# Clawd Clash

> A native macOS app (Swift + AppKit, no dependencies) that shows running Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Qwen Code, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI and pi sessions as pixel-art characters on the desktop or in a window, in one of several parody universes: Star Clawds (formerly Clawd Wars), Marvelous Clawds (formerly Clawdvengers: Clawd Wars), Detective Clawds (formerly Justice Clawds: Clawd Wars), Doctor Clawd (time travel), The Clawd Files (paranormal investigation), Stevie Clawdberg (the Spielberg and Amblin blockbusters), Clawd of the Rings (the hobbits, the Fellowship and the One Ring), Clawd Slayer (Buffy the Vampire Slayer and its spin-off Angel), Stranger Clawds (Stranger Things, all five seasons), Superclawdtural (Supernatural: the Winchesters, the Impala and fifteen seasons of hunting things) or Clawds of the Universe (He-Man and She-Ra: Castle Greyskull, the Horde and the 1987 film). Every character, place and catchphrase has a parody name; code identifiers and comments still use the originals. A scene never mixes universes, except in Clawd Royale. Every session and subagent is a hero or a villain; they fight while they work. Status comes from the AIs' hooks (one hook binary, `--assistant codex|qwen|gemini|copilot|pi` and `--event <name>`; per-AI config in `HookInstaller.OtherAI`, payloads translated by `StatusStore.normalize`). Every sprite, effect, location and the app icon are drawn in code; there are no image assets.

- Universes: `Sources/Shared/Universe.swift` (ids: universe base + villain 0..<100 / hero 100+, cast sizes, agent-only, rivals, Claude's side; `adopt` maps ids across universes; the status file records the universe on show, the hook casts from it). `Roster` is who can be cast: one universe, or all of them in Clawd Royale (`StatusFile.mixed`, `SaverFeed.mixed`, `Universe.mixed` in the app, UserDefaults `clawdRoyale`, `--clawd-royale` for a test run); in Clawd Royale nobody is recast and `Universe.shown` is the universe of the place on show. `Sources/App/Theme.swift`: a universe's content (cast personas, places, homes, nemeses, rides, menu icon, legend). `Sources/App/Universes/StarClawds`, `/MarvelousClawds`, `/DetectiveClawds`, `/DoctorClawd`, `/ClawdFiles`, `/StevieClawdberg`, `/ClawdOfTheRings`, `/Slayer` and `/StrangerClawds` hold each theme (roster, Art/, Places/; Star Clawds' file names start with `StarClawds`, Detective Clawds' with `Detective`, Doctor Clawd's with `Doctor`, The Clawd Files' with `Files`, Stevie Clawdberg's with `Clawdberg`, Clawd of the Rings' with `Rings` and Clawd Slayer's with `Slayer` and Stranger Clawds' with `Hawkins`, since Swift needs unique file names; Clawd Slayer's enum case is `Universe.slayer`, key `slayer`, and its top-level names and place keys all start with `slayer`/`Slayer`; Stranger Clawds' is `Universe.hawkins`, key `hawkins`, its names and place keys starting with `hawkins`/`Hawkins`). Marvel, DC, Doctor Clawd, The Clawd Files, Stevie Clawdberg, Clawd of the Rings and Clawd Slayer and Stranger Clawds change place with transitions of their own (`MarvelousComicTrip`, `DetectiveComicTrip`, `DoctorTrip`, `FilesTrip`, `ClawdbergTrip`, `RingsTrip`, `SlayerTrip`, whose thirteen kinds are `SlayerWipe`, each drawn in its own `Slayer…Trip.swift`, and `HawkinsTrip`, whose ten kinds are `HawkinsWipe`, each drawn in its own `Hawkins…Trip.swift` and ending on Joyce's Christmas lights spelling the new place's name, `HawkinsLights.swift`), picked through `Universes/ComicTransition.swift`; The Clawd Files' place names also type themselves in after each change (`FilesCaption`). Doctor Clawd also has the TARDIS (`Ride.tardis`, which materialises instead of flying in), the Weeping Angle that only moves while nobody faces it (Overlay's tick), and regeneration: Claude Code's `PreCompact` hook moves a Doctor's session to the next Doctor (`Universe.regenerations`, `SessionRecord.regenerated`) and the overlay plays a golden flare (`DoctorRegeneration.swift`). The Clawd Files has its own rides (`Ride.sedan`, which drives in along the ground, `.helicopter`, `.saucer`) and missing time: the same `PreCompact` hook marks one of the seven FBI agents' sessions (`Universe.abductees`, `SessionRecord.abducted`) and the overlay lifts them away in a beam and sets them back down (`FilesMissingTime.swift`). Stevie Clawdberg has the DeLorean and the park jeep (which drive in), the moon bike and the mothership (`ClawdbergRides.swift`), and 88 mph: its time travellers are in `Universe.abductees` too, and the overlay plays `ClawdbergOutaTime` for them instead of the beam (`ClawdbergOutaTime.swift`); Indiana Bones and the Cairo Swordsman play Han shoots first (`Cast.isHan`, `ShootsFirst.says`); T. Wrecks's water glass and Captain Clawd's flinch are drawn by the overlay; its art files share `cb`-prefixed helpers (`ClawdbergKit.swift`). Clawd of the Rings has the Great Eagle (`drawEagle` in Rides.swift), which comes only for Gandclawd, Frodough and Samwise; `Universe.guises` keeps one character's two guises off the screen together and `Universe.homebound` keeps Smaug the Stashed on his hoard (`Roster.ruledOut`, `Roster.recast`, `StatusStore.at`); Shellob's signature climbs a thread up out of sight (`Persona.climb`, drawn by whoever places the sprite). Clawd Slayer has the school bus, Spike's DeSoto and Angel's convertible (`Ride.schoolBus`, `.deSoto`, `.gtx`, all of which drive in; `SlayerRides.swift`), and Tabula Rasa, its regeneration: the eight from that episode (Buffy, Willow, Xander, Giles, Anya, Tara, Spyke, Dawn) are in `Universe.abductees`, and when one's session compacts the overlay plays Willow's forgetting spell on the missing-time clock instead of the beam (`SlayerTabulaRasa.swift`: the crystal, the smoke, the "?" and a caption such as "JOAN?", then the crack and the shimmer; `--missing-time` in the Playground tests it). `SlayerHabits.swift` holds the rest: Hush (`slayerHushes`, `slayerHushed`: with the Gentlemen on stage every speech bubble comes up empty), the full moon worked out from the date (`slayerFullMoon`: Ozz and Veruka stay wolves; `slayerMoonOverride` for previews), the First Evil's guises (`slayerFirstEvilGuise`: the Old Master, the Mayor, Glory or Adam, whole, for a few seconds; `slayerForcedGuise` for previews) and the Mayor's wet wipe after every duel (`SlayerAfterDuel`, kept by the overlay and the screen saver). Angstel and Spyke are `Universe.rivals` (never lead two sessions back to back), only the witches meditate (`slayerWitches`, read by `Drills`), and its bespoke drills are `slayerBespokeDrills` (`SlayerDrills.swift`); its art files share `slayer`-prefixed helpers (`SlayerKit.swift`). Stranger Clawds has the Party's BMX bikes (`HawkinsRides.swift`: two friends ride in and the one leaving hops on the pegs), and Taken to the Upside Down for a compaction: the eight who've been there are in `Universe.abductees`, and the overlay pulls them back through a wall that stretches like a membrane and returns them slimy (`HawkinsTaken.swift`). `HawkinsHabits.swift` holds Eleven's nosebleed after a fight (an after-duel move, `StageQuirks.afterDuelFrom`), Vecna's grandfather clock looming behind the heroes and Steve telling the kids to stay close; Vecna and One are `Universe.rivals`, nobody meditates, its bespoke drills are in `HawkinsDrills.swift`, its art files share `hawkins`-prefixed helpers (`HawkinsKit.swift`), and the kids stand lower than the teenagers and grown-ups (`hawkinsKidDrop`). `Universe.isReleased` and `Universe.offered` are what people can pick: Settings, Random, Clawd Royale and the saver's Options read them. `Universe.shown` is the universe on show in this process; the screen saver picks its own from its Options sheet (`SaverView.choice`). Clawds of the Universe (`Sources/App/Universes/Eternia/`, prefix `Eternia`, key `eternia`) has the Wind Raider, Swift Wind, the Roton, the Horde skiff and Hordakk's rocket (`EterniaRides.swift`), and the transformation for a compaction (`compaction: .transform`): Prince Addam, Adorra, Cringer and Spirit are `Universe.guises` with He-Clawd, She-Clawd, Battle Kat and Swift Wind, and `PreCompact` swaps the leader to its other guise unless that one is on stage (`SessionRecord.transformed`; the flash and the line are `EterniaPower.swift`'s `Transformation`, `--transform` in the Playground). Its heroes now and then give the moral of the story when they finish (`UniverseFacts.morals`, `SessionRecord.moral`, `--moral`). Its twelve trips are `EterniaTrip`, each in its own `Eternia…Trip.swift`, ending on a stone caption (`EterniaStone.swift`); its habits, with Skeleclawd's retreat as an after-duel move, are in `EterniaHabits.swift` and its bespoke drills in `EterniaDrills.swift`. Star Wars draws guns, flashes and smoke as Clawd Wars did (`classic` in Pose.swift) and keeps Han shoots first (`Universes/StarClawds/ShootsFirst.swift`).

## Build and run

- Requirements: macOS 13+ on Apple silicon, Swift 6.2+ from either the Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`) or Xcode, compiled in Swift 5 language mode. No third-party dependencies. Signing falls back to ad-hoc, which is fine locally (macOS then drops the Accessibility grant on every rebuild).
- The type checker's limit on a single expression is fixed, not timed, so a faster machine or a retry won't get past it. When the build fails with "unable to type-check this expression in reasonable time", the other errors in that file (`cannot infer contextual base`, key paths, `Float16` operators) all come from that one expression. Fix it by stating types: array literals of hex colours as `[Int]`, angles and closure parameters as `Double`. Write new art code the same way. Long untyped literal arrays piped through `.map`, and `.pi` arithmetic without an annotated `let`, are what trip it.
- `./build.sh` compiles with `swiftc` (no Xcode project, no SwiftPM), signs, installs `/Applications/Clawd Clash.app`, runs `--update-hooks` (refreshes only the AIs already connected; it never connects a new one, the app asks for that) and launches it. `./build.sh --no-hooks` skips the hooks. `./build.sh --no-install` builds, quits any running copy (only one runs at a time) and launches `build/Clawd Clash.app`: no copy to /Applications, no hook refresh (a build/ copy never takes over working hooks, see `HookInstaller.repairMoved`). `./build.sh --no-install --dev-tools` (never on by default, and only together with `--no-install`, so it's never installed or released) also compiles the `--jump=<pid>` and `--ax-dump=<pid>` click-to-jump diagnostics (`#if CLAWD_DEV_TOOLS` in main.swift). `./build.sh --untrusted` is for trying someone's PR: signed ad hoc (none of the installed app's permissions), never installed or launched, no hooks touched. Every build is signed with the hardened runtime. `--install-hooks` connects every installed AI (Claude Code, Codex, Qwen Code, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, pi). An installed AI you don't connect can be waved off with the banner's × or "Don't Remind Me About …" (`OverlayController.ignoredHooks`).
- Pull requests are checked by `scripts/pr-guard.py` (CI: `.github/workflows/pr-guard.yml`, `pull_request_target`, so main's copy of the guard runs and the PR's code is only read as text). It sorts changed files into green (a universe's folder, docs pictures, README, CHANGELOG), yellow (everything else, for review) and red (build and release scripts, dotfiles, AI instructions including this file, the hook and `Sources/Shared/{StatusStore,Processes,GitRemote,SaverFeed}`, `HookInstaller`/`SaverInstaller`/`Jump`/`main`, new core files). Added lines in universe folders may not use file, process, network, app or environment APIs, may import only Foundation/CoreGraphics/CoreText/AppKit, and new non-private top-level names must start with the universe's prefix (`PREFIXES` in the script, or `<Prefix>Roster.swift`). Rules for contributors: `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- `./release.sh` works out the next version (`scripts/next-version.sh`: a new universe raises the middle number, anything else the last; the first stays at 4), builds an Apple silicon (arm64) release zip, publishes it as a GitHub release and updates the Homebrew cask in `rodclemen/homebrew-tap`.
- There are no unit tests; `<app binary> --chaos=90` is a randomized soak test of the layout (characters on screen, nobody stuck walking, nobody missing, labels on screen and not overlapping) that prints a report and exits non-zero on violations. Check visuals with the frame dump: `CLAWD_SHOT=/tmp/shot.png <app binary> --playground=0,1 --agents=0,1 [--mood=idle] [--ais=claude,codex] [--projects=a,a,b]` writes the rendered scene every 5 s (window mode is the default; `defaults write <domain> windowMode -bool false` for the desktop). `CLAWD_HOVER=<actor key>` fakes a hover; `VADER_DEBUG=1` logs layout and fight roles.
- `Tools/RenderDocs` renders each universe's `docs/roster-<slug>.png`, `docs/locations-<slug>.png`, `docs/desktop-<slug>.png` and `docs/social-preview-<slug>.png`; `Tools/MakeSocial` renders Clawd Clash's own `docs/social-preview.png`; `Tools/MakeIcon` renders `Resources/AppIcon.png`.
- `Tools/Preview/build.sh` builds `build/preview`, the art workbench: `cast out.png <names|batch|universe|all>` (every pose: idle, walk/flight, working, fight, hit, waiting, sitting, weapon habit, signature ¼ ½ ¾; batches are the Art files' dictionaries, `heroes1`, `dcVillains3`, `ringsHeroes2`…), `fight out.png a b` (a fight with its effects over time), `drills out.png <names>` (solo practice sets), `magic out.png [names]` (every magic stream side by side), `place out.png <places|all>` (window strip and screen-saver size), `rides out.png`.

## Code map

- [Sources/Shared/StatusStore.swift](Sources/Shared/StatusStore.swift): the state shared by hook and app (`~/.claude/clawd-clash/state.json`, written under `flock`). Turns hook events into session/agent records, assigns characters (`side(for:in:)`: Claude Code takes the heroes when another AI runs), and builds `SessionSnapshot`s. A session's project name comes from its live process cwd (not the hooks' copy, which goes stale after a folder rename): the git remote's repo name, else the folder name.
- [Sources/Shared/Processes.swift](Sources/Shared/Processes.swift): finds `claude`, `codex`, `qwen`, `gemini`, `copilot` and `pi` processes, their cwd, start time and CPU time (sessions without hooks, dead-session pruning, "busy" detection).
- [Sources/Shared/GitRemote.swift](Sources/Shared/GitRemote.swift): reads a project's remote from `.git/config` on disk (no network; walks up from subfolders, follows worktrees), giving the repo name and host label for the card pill. Cached per cwd, re-read every 5 s.
- [Sources/Hook/main.swift](Sources/Hook/main.swift): the `clawd-clash-hook` binary every connected AI runs (`HookInstaller.isOurs` recognises it, and the replaced apps' hooks, by the exact file name a hook command runs); reads hook JSON from stdin, never prints, always exits 0.
- [Sources/App/Overlay.swift](Sources/App/Overlay.swift): `OverlayController`: refresh loop, status debounce, fight pairing and formation layout, walking, labels, bubbles, hover cards, menus (incl. the menu bar icon, the universe's `Theme.menuIcon`), window-mode glue, frame dump. `OverlayView.render` draws a list of `DrawItem`s (screen coordinates).
- [Sources/App/Persona.swift](Sources/App/Persona.swift) and each universe's `Sources/App/Universes/*/<Prefix>Roster.swift`: the cast (`<Prefix>Hero` and `<Prefix>Villain` enums such as `DoctorHero`/`DoctorVillain`; append only, ids are stored), `Persona` (name, `Weapon` (`.saber` = melee, `.blaster` = ranged, `.lightning` = magic), `Motion` fly/hover/swing/walk, `ShotStyle`, `Magic` colours and look (forked, ray, rings, waves, spell, `touch`, `rcCar`; `Theme.persona` fills in `Magic.variant` from `magicVariants` so no two characters draw the same stream; `build/preview magic` shows them all), armour, muzzle, pivot, `bulk` for duel spacing, headTop, signature length, callout, the drawing function), homes (`Location.<prefix>Home(of:)`, e.g. `doctorHome`), arch-enemies (`Cast.nemeses`, paired first in fights) and ship pickups (`Cast.ride`).
- [Sources/App/Universes/*/Art/](Sources/App/Universes): the art. Each universe's `<Prefix>Heroes1…N.swift` and `<Prefix>Villains1…N.swift` (Marvel's are plain `Heroes`/`Villains`) register a dictionary of personas (`doctorHeroes1`…, merged in the universe's roster) next to their private drawing functions; `Sources/App/Rides.swift` draws the shared ships (the Falcon, Quinjet, Milano, Javelin, Batwing, TARDIS, Great Eagle), and The Clawd Files, Stevie Clawdberg and Clawd Slayer draw theirs in their own `*Rides.swift`. Each file is self-contained, so batches can be drawn independently.
- [Sources/App/Pose.swift](Sources/App/Pose.swift): one drawing pipeline for everyone. `drawPersona` turns mood, fight role, idle habit, walking/flying and sitting into a `Pose`, calls the persona's drawing function, then draws the shared effects (muzzle flash and solo shots with `drawProjectile`, magic streams with `drawMagic`, smoke). Its header comment is the contract for drawing functions. Hoverers are lifted in here; flyers get `p.flying`.
- [Sources/App/Characters.swift](Sources/App/Characters.swift): shared sprite helpers: the Clawd body (`Look`, `drawLegs`, `drawBody`), palette, `noise`, the swing choreography (`kataPose`, `duelPose`, `saberTrail`), `drawSaber`, `drawHood`, `drawPistol`.
- [Sources/App/Fights.swift](Sources/App/Fights.swift): `VaderMode`, `FightRole`s and `fightRoles`, the shoot-out outcomes, fight effects between two `Fighter`s (`drawFightFX`; `Fighter.dressed(as:)` gives it the character's shots and magic), `drawCape`, speech bubbles.
- [Sources/App/Locations.swift](Sources/App/Locations.swift) and [Sources/App/Universes/*/Places/](Sources/App/Universes): `Location` (213 places across the universes) looks up a `Place` (name, panel tint, still layer, optional moving layer) registered in each universe's `<Prefix>Scenes1…N.swift`; Locations.swift keeps the wipe and the shared scene helpers (`gradient`, `stars`, `ground`, `Scenes.Pen`, `isTall`/`unit` for the screen saver's full-screen canvases).
- Flight and swinging are in `OverlayController`: `Actor.air` eases 0…1 as a flyer sets off and lands and lifts it by `flightHeight`; Spider-Man's arc and web line (`webLine`) are computed from his x. A departing flyer rises instead of sinking; a character with a `ride` is picked up by its ship (`falconItem`, `drawRide`).
- [Sources/App/WindowMode.swift](Sources/App/WindowMode.swift): the window (themed header, scene strip, per-Claude cards, auto height). `RoomView` holds the location's static picture behind `SceneView`.
- [Sources/App/SpriteLayers.swift](Sources/App/SpriteLayers.swift): shows a frame's `DrawItem`s as reused Core Animation layers (GPU scaling, nearest-neighbour; text cached as images), for both the window's scene and the desktop crew. `OverlayView.render` is still the Core Graphics path, used for text images and `CLAWD_SHOT`.
- [Sources/App/Jump.swift](Sources/App/Jump.swift): click-to-jump to a session's terminal tab or editor window (AppleScript for Terminal/iTerm2, Accessibility API for VS Code/Cursor incl. native tabs).
- Hook health: `OverlayController.refreshStatus` lists `hookIssues` for AIs that are installed (`HookInstaller.claudeAvailable` / `available`) but not hooked up, or whose sessions ran a turn without reporting (`SessionSnapshot.hookSilent`, e.g. Codex hooks not approved in `/hooks`). These feed the banner, ⚠︎ menu items and a one-per-session notification.
- [Sources/Saver/SaverView.swift](Sources/Saver/SaverView.swift): the screen saver (`Clawd Clash.saver`, built by build.sh into the app's Resources), and the window's third view (the app compiles it in too: `ClawdWindow.board`, fed `OverlayController.saverFeed` through `feedSource`, `inWindow` for no clock, a bigger place name and hover-to-enlarge cards). A `ScreenSaverView` running sandboxed in macOS's `legacyScreenSaver` host: the location at full screen (about 270 art pixels tall), the crew with the window's fight pairing, name tags over every head (`Cast.drawnTop` / `drawnProfile` measure each sprite, shared with the window's labels; the focused session's tag is 15% larger), one card per session floating above the crew in its project's colour with a beam to its name (`board`), the clock and an event ticker, all as Core Animation layers. Every 10 minutes (`shiftEvery`) it wipes to another location (`travel`, `Wipe` in Locations.swift, shared with the window) and swaps the clock and place name and lifts the cards and tags (`shifted`) against burn-in. It reads only [Sources/Shared/SaverFeed.swift](Sources/Shared/SaverFeed.swift)'s `screensaver.json` in `~/Library/Application Support/Clawd Clash/`, which the running app writes about once a second while the saver is installed (`OverlayController.publishSaverFeed`); stale = the app isn't running (never in the window, which hands it the feed directly), and the saver puts on a show instead: a made-up crew of 4–6 (`cast(for:)`, up to two of them agents, heroes against villains, a local or two of the place among them) with name tags but no cards, off somewhere new every 3 minutes (`demoEvery`), and a quiet "isn't running" line under the place name. Inside the sandbox `NSHomeDirectory()` is the container: use `SaverFeed.home`. [Sources/App/SaverInstaller.swift](Sources/App/SaverInstaller.swift) copies it into `~/Library/Screen Savers`, refreshes that copy when the app's differs (code or sealed resources), and removes it. Locations draw extra scenery only on tall canvases, so the window's strip is unchanged.
- [Sources/App/Habits.swift](Sources/App/Habits.swift): idle habits. `Cast.habits` picks what a character does while idle and standing (glance, shuffle, bounce, or its weapon habit: flourish, checkWeapon, crackle); `Cast.draw` sets the global `idleHabit` for `drawPersona` and applies the whole-sprite ones (mirror, shift) afterwards. A new character gets habits from its weapon automatically; a ranged character with `handGun: false` (repulsors, optic blasts) skips the gun check. Signature moves: give the persona a `signature` length (seconds) and draw it while `p.signature` (0…1) is non-nil. `forcedHabit` plays a chosen one for previews.
- [Sources/App/Legend.swift](Sources/App/Legend.swift): Status Symbols (top level of the menu), the key to bubbles, poses, outline and label colours and banners. Icons come from the real drawing code (`drawPersona`, `drawBubble`, `drawFocusCaret`), so a new bubble kind or status should get a row here and in the README's table. Rows are custom views: macOS 27 menus ignore `NSMenuItem.image`.
- [Sources/App/HookInstaller.swift](Sources/App/HookInstaller.swift), [Sources/App/Accents.swift](Sources/App/Accents.swift), [Sources/App/Pixel.swift](Sources/App/Pixel.swift) (the `PixelCanvas` all art is drawn on).

## Conventions

- Sprites are 72×52 canvases facing right; the body is x 18…37, y 26…37, feet end at row 43, the hand pivot is (41.5, 34.5). Characters facing left are mirrored by the renderer. `C(0xRRGGBB)` makes a colour; `canvas.pattern(x, y, rows, palette)` draws string art.
- Adding a character: append a case to the universe's `<Prefix>Hero` or `<Prefix>Villain` (its roster file), register its `Persona` and drawing function in an Art file, give it a home in `Location.<prefix>Home(of:)`, and bump `heroCount`/`villainCount` in `Universe.swift`. Agent-only characters go in `Universe.agentOnly` (global ids). Check it with `build/preview`.
- Cast ids: `universe.base` (raw value × 1000) plus the villain's raw value (< 100) or `100 +` the hero's (`StatusStore.heroBase`); `Cast` (Sources/App/Cast.swift) wraps both and draws either as a session or an agent. Side rules live in `StatusStore.side(for:in:)`, `nextLeader` and `nextAgentCast`.
- Per-AI look lives in `AIStyle` (Sources/App/Accents.swift): outline colour (never dark) and list order. `Actor.assistant` carries it to sprites; cards and the menu group by it.
- Fight rules: arch-enemies (`Cast.nemeses`) face off first, whether each is a Claude or an agent (in `relayout` and the screen saver's `crew`); then Claudes fight Claudes, agents fight agents, a leftover Claude and agent fight each other, anyone else left over cheers; unarmed characters are bystanders.
- Commits follow Conventional Commits; every change gets a CHANGELOG entry.
